children.translated_text: First Section (<s>Niḥṣyanda</s>)
He by whose opening and closing of the eyes the world undergoes dissolution and arising —
that <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva), the source of the glory of the wheel of powers (<s>śakticakra</s>), we praise. || 1 ||

children.text: yatra sthitam idaṃ sarvaṃ kāryaṃ yasmāc ca nirgataṃ |
children.translated_text: In whom all this is established, from whom it has emerged —
because his form is never concealed, there is no obstruction [of him] anywhere. || 2 ||
Even in the difference between waking and other [states], that [<s>spanda</s>] flows forth, undivided [through them all];
it never turns away from its own nature, as the perceiver. || 3 ||

children.text: ahaṃ sukhī ca duḥkhī ca raktaś ca ityadisamvidaḥ |
children.translated_text: "I am happy," "I am suffering," "I am attached" — such cognitions (<s>saṃvid</s>)
are strung through the states of pleasure and the rest, but clearly they exist elsewhere [than in those states]. || 4 ||

children.text: na duḥkhaṃ na sukhaṃ yatra na grāhyam grāhakaṃ na ca |
children.translated_text: Where there is neither suffering nor pleasure, neither object nor subject,

children.text: na cāsti mūḍhabhāvo 'pi tad asti paramārthataḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: and where even the state of delusion does not exist — that exists in the highest sense (<s>paramārtha</s>). || 5 ||
Because this group of instruments [of cognition] (<s>karaṇavarga</s>), though deluded, [functions] as if undeluded, of its own accord,
together with the inner wheel [of powers], [there is] activity, maintenance, and dissolution. || 6 ||
One attains that reality to be examined through effort, with devotion,
because its freedom (<s>svatantratā</s>) is everywhere and unartificial. || 7 ||
It does not function as the impeller of one whose desire has not been aroused;

children.text: api tv ātmabalasparśāt puruṣas tatsamo bhavet || 8 ||
children.translated_text: but rather, through contact with the power of the Self (<s>ātmabala</s>), a person becomes equal to that. || 8 ||
For one who is incapable due to one's own impurity, though desirous of actions to be performed —

children.text: yadā kṣobhaḥ pralīyeta tadā syāt paramam padam || 9 ||
children.translated_text: when the agitation (<s>kṣobha</s>) subsides, then one attains the supreme state (<s>parama pada</s>). || 9 ||
Then his unartificial nature (<s>dharma</s>), characterized by the capacity of knowing and acting,

children.text: yatas tadepsitaṃ sarvaṃ jānāti ca karoti ca || 10 ||
children.translated_text: [manifests] — whereby he knows and does all that is desired. || 10 ||
One who, contemplating one's own nature as the presiding authority,

children.text: smayamāna ivāste yas tasyeyaṃ kusṛtiḥ kutaḥ || 11 ||
children.translated_text: remains as if smiling [in wonder] — for such a one, how could there be this wretched course [of transmigration]? || 11 ||

children.text: nābhāvo bhāvyatām eti na ca tatrāsty amūḍhatā |
children.translated_text: Non-existence does not become the object of contemplation, nor is there non-delusion therein;
because from the contact of effort [upon awakening], there is the certainty that "it existed" [during deep sleep]. || 12 ||
Therefore, that [state of deep sleep] should always be known as artificial, like the state of deep sleep [itself];

children.text: na tv evaṃ smaryamāṇatvaṃ tat tattvam pratipadyate || 13 ||
children.translated_text: but not so that which is remembered — it does not experience that reality [directly]. || 13 ||
And there is a pair of states here, designated as the state of being an effect and the state of being an agent;

children.text: kāryatā kṣayiṇī tatra kartṛtvam punar akṣayam || 14 ||
children.translated_text: the state of being an effect is perishable, but the state of being an agent is imperishable. || 14 ||

children.text: kāryonmukhaḥ prayatno yaḥ kevalaṃ so 'tra lupyate |
children.translated_text: Only the effort directed toward effects perishes here;
when that perishes, the unwise one thinks: "I have perished." || 15 ||
But the inner state (<s>bhāva</s>) that is the abode of the quality of omniscience —
its dissolution can never occur, because of the non-apprehension of another [state that could destroy it]. || 16 ||
The experience of that [<s>spanda</s>] is constant, unfailing in the three states [of waking, dream, deep sleep];

children.text: nityaṃ syāt suprabuddhasya tadādyante parasya tu || 17 ||
children.translated_text: for the fully awakened one, it is always [present]; for the other, [only] at the beginning and end [of each cognition]. || 17 ||
United with the supreme power (<s>śakti</s>), whose nature is both knowledge and the known,

children.text: padadvaye vibhur bhāti tadanyatra tu cinmayaḥ || 18 ||
children.translated_text: the Lord (<s>vibhu</s>) shines forth in the two states [of waking and dream]; but in the other [deep sleep], he is pure consciousness (<s>cinmaya</s>). || 18 ||
The outflows (<s>niḥṣyanda</s>) of vibration of the <s>guṇas</s> and the rest, through their dependence on the universal vibration (<s>sāmānyaspanda</s>),
having attained their existence, constantly remain non-obstructive for the knower (<s>jña</s>). || 19 ||
But for those of unawakened intellect, these [outflows], intent on concealing one's own [true] state,
cast [one] down onto the terrible, hard-to-cross path of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration). || 20 ||
Therefore, one who is constantly engaged in discerning the reality of <s>spanda</s> (vibration),
in the waking state itself, swiftly attains one's own [true] nature. || 21 ||

children.text: atikruddhaḥ prahṛṣṭo vā kiṃ karomīti vā mṛśan |
children.translated_text: Extremely enraged, or overjoyed, or deliberating "what shall I do?",

children.text: dhāvan va yat padaṃ gacchet tatra spandaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ || 22 ||
children.translated_text: or running — whatever state one reaches, there <s>spanda</s> is established. || 22 ||

children.text: yām avasthāṃ samālambya yad ayam mama vakṣyati |
children.translated_text: "Having taken hold of a particular state, this [<s>spanda</s>] will declare to me [what I should do]" —
resolving thus, "I shall certainly do that," one remains [firmly established]. || 23 ||
Taking hold of that [resolution], both the moon and the sun (<s>candra</s> and <s>sūrya</s>) [i.e., the two breaths], through the upward path,
in the <s>suṣumnā</s> channel, having set and left the realm of <s>brahmāṇḍa</s> (the cosmic egg) — || 24 ||
then, in that great void (<s>mahāvyoman</s>), when the moon and sun have dissolved,
the deluded one [remains] as in the state of deep sleep, but the awakened one becomes uncovered (<s>anāvṛta</s>). || 25 ||
Second Section (<s>Niḥṣyanda</s>)
Having taken hold of that power, <s>mantras</s>, endowed with the power of omniscience,
function for the purpose [of the practitioner], like the sense organs of embodied beings. || 1 ||
Therein they dissolve, [becoming] peaceful in form, stainless,
together with the mind of the worshipper — therefore they are of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>. || 2 ||
Since the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>) is constituted of everything, because of the arising of all states [within it],
through the form of the experience of that [totality], there is the realization of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>). || 3 ||

children.text: tasmāc chabdārthacintāsu na sāvasthā na yā śivaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the contemplation of word and object, there is no state that is not <s>Śiva</s>;
the experiencer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>) himself, in the form of what is experienced (<s>bhogya</s>), is always established everywhere. || 4 ||

children.text: iti vā yasya saṃvittiḥ krīḍātvenākhilaṃ jagat |
children.translated_text: Or, he whose consciousness [perceives] the entire world as play (<s>krīḍā</s>) —

children.text: sa paśyan satataṃ yukto jīvanmukto na saṃśayaḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: he, seeing thus, constantly united (<s>yukta</s>), is <s>jīvanmukta</s> (liberated while living), without doubt. || 5 ||
This indeed is the rising of that which is to be meditated upon (<s>dhyeya</s>) in the mind of the meditator —
the attainment of identity with that (<s>tadātmatāsamāpatti</s>), for the practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>) who desires it. || 6 ||
This itself is the attainment of immortality (<s>amṛta</s>), this itself is the grasping of the Self (<s>ātman</s>);
this is the initiation into <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the bestower of the true nature of <s>Śiva</s>. || 7 ||
Third Flow (<s>niḥṣyanda</s>)
accomplishes the objects present in the heart of the waking person for the embodied being, || 1 ||
Just as the Ordainer (<s>dhātā</s>), entreated according to one's wish, having caused the rise of the moon (<s>soma</s>) and sun (<s>sūrya</s>),
so in dream too, by virtue of not transgressing that affection (<s>praṇaya</s>),
stationed always more clearly in the center, he necessarily reveals the desired objects. || 2 ||

children.text: anyathā tu svatantrā syāt sṛṣṭis taddharmakatvataḥ |
children.translated_text: Otherwise, creation would be autonomous, being of its own nature,
always like that of a worldly person, in the two states of waking and dream. || 3 ||

children.text: yathā hi artho 'sphuṭo dṛṣṭaḥ sāvadhāne 'pi cetasi |
children.translated_text: Just as an object seen unclearly, even with an attentive mind,
shines forth more clearly again when cultivated through the exertion of one's own power, || 4 ||

children.text: tathā yat paramārthena yena yatra yathā sthitam |
children.translated_text: so too, that which is established in ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>), wherever and however it abides —

children.text: tat tathā balam ākramya na cirāt sampravartate || 5 ||
children.translated_text: having seized that power (<s>bala</s>), it manifests before long. || 5 ||
Even a weak person, having seized that [power], engages in action;

children.text: ācchādayed bubhukṣāṃ ca tathā yo 'ti bubhukṣitaḥ || 6 ||
children.translated_text: and similarly, one who is very hungry can cover over his hunger. || 6 ||
Just as in a body presided over by this [<s>spanda</s>], omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) and other [powers arise],
so from being established in one's own Self, it will be thus everywhere. || 7 ||
Languor (<s>glāni</s>) is the dullness of the body, and its arising is from ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>);

children.text: tad unmeṣaviluptaṃ cet kutaḥ sā syād ahetukā || 8 ||
children.translated_text: if that is dissolved by the unfolding (<s>unmeṣa</s>) [of <s>spanda</s>], how could it exist without a cause? || 8 ||
The arising of another [state] for one absorbed in a single thought —

children.text: unmeṣaḥ sa tu vijñeyaḥ svayaṃ tam upalakṣayet || 9 ||
children.translated_text: that is to be known as the unfolding (<s>unmeṣa</s>); one should observe it oneself. || 9 ||

children.text: ato bindur ato nādo rūpam asmād ato rasaḥ |
children.translated_text: From this, the point (<s>bindu</s>); from this, the sound (<s>nāda</s>); form from this; from this, taste —
they manifest very quickly, as agitators of the embodied being. || 10 ||
When, as if desiring to see, one pervades all objects and abides [in them] —

children.text: tadā kiṃ bahunoktena svayam eva avabhotsyate || 11 ||
children.translated_text: then what need of saying more? One will know for oneself. || 11 ||
One should always remain awakened (<s>prabuddha</s>), illuminating one's field of experience (<s>gocara</s>) with knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>);
one should deposit everything in one [place] — then one is not afflicted by another. || 12 ||
He who has gone to the state of being an enjoyer of the group of powers (<s>śaktivarga</s>) arising from the mass of words (<s>śabdarāśi</s>),

children.text: kalāviluptavibhavo gataḥ san sa paśuḥ smṛtaḥ || 13 ||
children.translated_text: having lost his splendor through the <s>kalās</s> (limited phases) — he is called a <s>paśu</s> (bound soul). || 13 ||
The loss of the taste of the supreme nectar (<s>parāmṛtarasa</s>), which is his arising from conditions (<s>pratyaya</s>) —
through that he enters unfreedom (<s>asvatantratā</s>), and that [condition] has only the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) as its object. || 14 ||
And his powers (<s>śakti</s>), constantly arising for the concealment of his own nature —
because without the penetration of word (<s>śabdānuvedha</s>), there is no arising of conditions. || 15 ||
This very power, of the nature of action (<s>kriyā</s>), belonging to <s>Śiva</s> but abiding in the <s>paśu</s> (bound soul),
is binding when on one's own path; when known, it bestows <s>siddhi</s> (perfection). || 16 ||
Confined by the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (subtle body of eight), abiding in mind (<s>manas</s>), ego (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>), and intellect (<s>buddhi</s>),
in the form of the arising of the <s>tanmātras</s>, one is generated from conditions. || 17 ||

children.text: bhuṅkte paravaśo bhogaṃ tadbhāvāt saṃsared ataḥ |
children.translated_text: Subject to another's power, one enjoys experience (<s>bhoga</s>); from that state one transmigrates;
we shall explain the cause of the dissolution of this <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration). || 18 ||

children.text: yadā tv ekatra saṃrūḍhas tadā tasya layodayau |
children.translated_text: But when one is firmly established in one [principle], then, controlling its dissolution and arising,

children.text: niyacchan bhoktṛtām eti tataś cakreśvaro bhavet || 19 ||
children.translated_text: one attains the status of the enjoyer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>), and thereby becomes the Lord of the Wheel (<s>cakreśvara</s>). || 19 ||
Fourth Flow (<s>niḥṣyanda</s>)
I praise that [speech] — the boat for crossing over the unfathomable ocean of doubt,
that wonderful speech of the <s>guru</s>, with words of marvelous meaning. || 1 ||
Having obtained this unobtainable treasure of knowledge (<s>jñānadhana</s>), deposited in the cave of the heart —

children.text: vasuguptavac chivāya hi bhavati sadā sarvalokasya || 2 ||
children.translated_text: like <s>Vasugupta</s>, it always serves for the welfare (<s>śiva</s>) of all the world. || 2 ||
